What happens to my Crypto exchanges (Coinbase) when I die?

Short answer: Crypto held on Coinbase becomes part of your estate. Your executor can claim it through Coinbase's executor process with a death certificate, proof of legal authority (such as probate) and ID. Coinbase doesn't support beneficiary designations, so heirs need to know the account exists.

What to do

  1. List every exchange account in your digital estate plan, without passwords in your will.
  2. After a death, the executor submits Coinbase's estate claim with a death certificate, probate documents and ID.
  3. The receiving person may need their own Coinbase account for the transfer.
  4. Self-custody wallets are different: without the seed phrase the funds are lost, so see crypto inheritance tools.

Read the official policy ↗

FAQ

Can I name a beneficiary on Coinbase?

No. The assets pass according to your will or the law.

What about crypto in a hardware wallet?

No company can recover it. Your heirs need the seed phrase or an inheritance setup.
